coverage_note: No echo-candidates file was supplied, so no echo notes. The engine garbled several of Amal's lines: 16:49 'فئة واحدة؟' is probably 'غيمة واحدة؟'; 20:12 and 20:30 'يوم' = 'غيم'; 32:14 'زعلتكش عن' = 'غير عن'; 43:06 'بهدئ' = 'بيحرق'; 47:24 'وحدات؟' is unclear, maybe 'وردات؟'. Latin stretches on Medi's side: 03:07 'amalit tilha' (he fixed it himself, not filed); 04:49 'alayhi salmik' = 'allah ysalmek' (pronunciation, not filed); 05:39 'fin tain el tod' = 'tentain illa tult' (he fixed his 'تلات إلا تلت' himself, not filed); 30:11 'maratat'; 46:03 'nadafti nadafet'. Not filed: 05:51 he echoed her 'لسه عندكم shoab?' as 'لسه هون شوب؟' (a mishearing, then he asked for it again); 06:52 قلقان→قلقانين and 30:36 مرة→مرات (he fixed them himself first); 21:04 طيار→طيارة (self-fix); 50:27 حجار (self-fix); 44:20 'nar heret me' (he was repeating her line); 04:07 and 32:47 (repeats of her fixes). Lines 1:04:11 to 1:07:00 are English talk about the app. No tier-3 rows: 'dangerous', 'cough' and 'PTT' are not on her sheet.

rows.why: He was talking about his fiancée and used the masculine adjective; Amal recast it as feminine عيانة.
After her 02:00 fix he said the masculine form again, and she fixed it again (عيانة), so this is its own slip; he then said 'Yeah, عيانة'.
rows.english: My fiancée is a bit sick

rows.why: He gave the verb with no subject and tacked راسها on afterwards; Amal recast the order with راسها before the verb. This is the brief's own example, and his 04:07 line is a repeat.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He asked how to say cough and Amal supplied كحة, so this is a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: No, you can use the adjective. Or I worry.
rows.why: For 'we are worried' he offered the verb as a question; Amal said no, use the adjective, and he built احنا قلقانين. This may be a rule question rather than a slip.

rows.medi_said: الـ or لا الـ نار. ... لـ النار for fire
rows.why: He put la- after قلقان; Amal said 'Men not', and قلقان takes من.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another verb for a fire starting; Amal did not give it)
rows.why: He tried 'start' for a fire breaking out; Amal said no, that needs another word, and set it aside.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for? I don't know how to say this right.
rows.why: He asked how to say 'take care of' and Amal supplied دير بالي, so this is a didn't-know.
He dropped the على that دير بال takes and the -i ending on بال; Amal recast it as بالي على خطيبتي.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée

rows.why: He left out على again two minutes after her fix, and she named the rule again, so this is a fresh slip.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée

rows.medi_said: ديرت بالي على خطيبتي كل الصباح.
rows.why: Her sheet has 'morning | el-sube7' and she typed kul el-subu7; he used the formal الصباح. She voiced nothing (my reading).

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: Asked for another example, he built a malformed command with a wrong ending (باليك); Amal gave دير بالك and named it as the command form.
After خلينا (let's) the verb must be the bare present; he used the past عملنا, Amal said نعمل, and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه، uh, إنه تخطط-- uh, تخططي.
rows.why: He used إنه for the relative 'that', which should be اللي, and the present for 'you planned'; Amal only asked what he meant and did not fix it (my reading).

rows.medi_said: Oh, is it, is it، is it عصافير؟
rows.why: He could not recall 'sky' and guessed aloud (أسف, عصافير); Amal said عصافير is birds and supplied سما after his 'أنا نسيته'.
Her line is probably 'غيمة واحدة؟' (engine wrote فئة); it prompted the plural and he answered غيوم. Note that غيم as a collective noun is not clearly wrong.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.why: He understood her بتطلع as بتتطلع (look at); Amal said no and explained, and he said 'Oh, بتطلع, not بتتطلع'.

rows.medi_said: أنا نسيت الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: فجر. You could have just said الصبح بكير
rows.why: He produced a non-word (سجر) for 'dawn' after guessing Azan; Amal supplied فجر and he asked 'فجر or سجر?'.
He said 'غير لو' for 'other than'; Amal said 'No لو', just غير.

rows.medi_said: غير الشمس و غيوم شو، شو في.
rows.why: Amal recast it without el- (engine wrote يوم for غيم), and he then asked 'غير never takes...?'.
rows.english: other than the sun and clouds, what is there

rows.medi_said: So غير شم- غير شمس الـ، الغيوم
rows.why: Right after her model 'غير شمس و غيم' he put el- on the second noun after غير; she let it pass (my reading).

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme
rows.why: He built 'night sky' in English order with a bare سما (at 21:32 'ليل سما'); Amal recast it as السما بالليل and he repeated it.

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme
rows.why: He could not produce 'dark(ness)' and Amal supplied عتمة, so this is a didn't-know.
'One' normally follows the noun (شمس وحدة); Amal only echoed واحدة and praised him (my reading).
نجمة is feminine, so after the noun taani needs the feminine form; she echoed تاني as a prompt and he changed it to تانية.
The fronted object نجمة needs a pointer ending on the verb; Amal named the pointer rule and he said 'بشوفها... I forgot the pointer rule'.

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He guessed لسا and then لا for 'since' as questions; Amal said no to both and supplied من.
He offered the I-form; Amal gave the feminine بتمطر (because of الدنيا/سما). It was phrased as a question, so it may not count.

rows.chat: min awal el-yoam, mattarat talat marraat
rows.why: He could not form the past 'it rained' and Amal supplied مطرت; it could be a tongue-twister stumble, as she suggested.
He said 'the first' for 'the air'; when he asked 'What I say?' Amal answered الأول, which confirms the engine heard him right.

rows.medi_said: آآ، غير من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: 'Different from' is 8eir + 3an; Amal gave عن (engine garbled her line) and he said 'غير always takes عن'.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time.
rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: aa5er + el- means 'the end of'; Amal explained this and he switched to آخر مرة.
The subject مرة is feminine; Amal prompted 'مرة is...' and he fixed it to كانت.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي for 'ago'; Amal said no, 'ago' is قبل + number + noun.
He said 'teeth' instead of 'years'; Amal asked what سنان is, he said teeth, and she supplied سنين.

rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: The past form came out with a long final vowel and no doubled letter; Amal recast تَلَّجَت. This is mostly sound shape.

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ ... Tell me it was very strong.
rows.why: 'The wind came a lot' did not make sense to her; she asked what it means twice and gave him 'was very strong', which he then built.
rows.english: The wind was very strong in the morning

rows.why: The object 'it' (الأرض) is missing from the verb; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said nadafetha.

rows.medi_said: Is it the bee? Is it the bee plants?
rows.amal_said: زبيب؟ ... Z-z-zبيب is raisins, I think. ... زريعة.
rows.why: He was groping for 'plants' and Amal supplied زريعة.
He guessed 'sand' for 'dirt'; Amal said it means sand, and he then found تراب himself.

rows.medi_said: I don't, أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: He could not recall 'stone' and Amal supplied حجر, so this is a didn't-know.
He meant 'streets' but used the singular with a feminine adjective; Amal recast it as the plural الشوارع.
An adjective after a definite noun takes el-; Amal added it and he repeated الإدام.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: He rendered 'made of' with a verb plus مع (with); Amal recast it as a bare حجر ('are stone') and said 'made of' is different from 'made'.
rows.english: The old streets in America are (made of) stone

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: noun + taani means 'another', not 'second'; Amal gave تاني حجر / الحجر التاني.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Standing alone, mufaddal takes el- plus 3ind, not a possessive ending; Amal explained this.

rows.medi_said: مفضل-- مفضل عندي أو مفضل لي يعني؟
rows.why: He repeated her form without el- and she prompted 'الـ' again; the repeat came out wrong, so it counts as its own slip.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: He put the adjective before the noun; Amal said المفضل is an adjective and goes after.
A noun with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal said 'No ال first'.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: For 'this lesson is my favorite' he gave a bare مفضل; Amal said it is an adjective that follows الدرس and takes el-.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في ('there is') as 'is'; Amal said في is 'there is' and gave مش هون. This could also be read as vocab, في instead of هون.
A mangled set phrase; Amal answered with her own يعطيك العافية rather than correcting him (my reading).
